studyInfo: Mouse spinal brain tissue from an experimental model of mitochondrial DNA double-strand break (mtDSB)–induced neuroinflammation. This model induces an 'inside-out' demyelination process driven by oligodendrocyte mitochondrial stress, leading to secondary activation of glial and immune populations and progressive neuroinflammatory lesion formation. The dataset includes multiple CNS cell types (oligodendrocytes, astrocytes, microglia, neurons) captured across different  stages to map the cellular and metabolic responses to mitochondrial dysfunction.
